items.topic: Scope: testing only or fix validation gap too?
items.context: validateGlobs uses filepath.Match for syntax checking, which silently accepts ** patterns it can never match at runtime. The actual runtime matching uses doublestar which does support **. This means validation is permissive — it won't reject patterns that would fail with filepath.Match semantics. Should we only add tests, or also fix the validator to use doublestar for syntax checking?

options.label: Tests only — document the gap
options.rationale: Lowest risk. The current behavior isn't broken (doublestar handles ** fine at runtime). Add tests that document the semantic difference.

options.label: Fix validator to use doublestar for syntax checking
options.rationale: More correct long-term. Ensures validation and runtime use the same library. Small blast radius since it only tightens validation.

items.topic: Test location for batch handler glob tests
items.context: Batch handler glob validation tests could go in the existing batch_handler_test.go or in a new dedicated glob test file. The existing file has other batch tests but zero glob coverage.

options.label: Add to batch_handler_test.go
options.rationale: Follows existing pattern — handler tests live alongside the handler they test. Consistent with how create/update handler tests are organized.

options.label: Create a dedicated globs_test.go
options.rationale: Groups all glob tests together for discoverability. Could consolidate cross-handler glob tests.

items.context: The spec.json has no acceptance_allow or acceptance_deny patterns set. Since this is a test-only change, the expected file changes are narrowly scoped to test files in the backlog package.

options.label: scenarios/swarm-manager/api/internal/backlog/**
options.rationale: Covers the backlog package where all handler and type tests live. Broad enough for any test file additions.

options.label: scenarios/swarm-manager/api/internal/backlog/*_test.go
options.rationale: More precise — only test files should change. But this pattern won't match if we also need to update types.go for a bug fix.

items.topic: How many validateGlobs edge cases to add?
items.context: Currently 7 test cases. The plan targets ≥12. Edge cases to consider: ** patterns, .. traversal, unicode, very long strings, nested brackets, trailing slashes, Windows-style separators.

options.label: Add 5-6 targeted edge cases (reach ~12-13 total)
options.rationale: Covers the most important gaps without over-testing. Focus on realistic patterns users would submit.

options.label: Add 10+ cases for exhaustive coverage (reach ~17+)
options.rationale: More thorough but diminishing returns. Some edge cases (unicode, very long strings) are unlikely in practice.

items.text: All existing glob tests pass. TestValidateGlobs has 7 cases, TestScenariosFromGlobs has 11 cases, and there are 4 execution service review-trigger tests. The pathutil and execution tests have good coverage — the gaps are specifically in the HTTP handler error paths and batch handler.

The validateGlobs function (types.go:146-161) rejects: empty patterns, absolute paths (starting with /), and syntactically invalid patterns (via filepath.Match). It does NOT reject: ** double-star patterns, relative path traversal (../), or patterns with special characters. This is by design — doublestar handles ** at runtime.

plan_updates: Created initial plan.md with 12 mandatory sections. Identified 4 key files needing new tests: types_test.go (edge cases), handler_test.go (error paths), batch_handler_test.go (both paths). Defined phased implementation strategy and definition of done.
